stem: In newborn screening, what do TRECs measure?

options.text: The production and development of new T-cells
The levels of maternal antibodies transferred in utero
The oxidative burst capacity of neonatal neutrophils
The presence of mutations in the JAK3 receptor

explanation: TRECs measure new T-cell production and thymic T-cell development. They are DNA byproducts formed during T-cell receptor gene rearrangement, so low levels suggest reduced thymic output.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because TRECs are DNA byproducts created during T-cell receptor gene rearrangement, so they reflect thymic T-cell production and maturation.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because maternal antibodies are not what TRECs measure in newborn screening.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because TRECs assess T-cell development, not neutrophil oxidative burst function.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because TRECs do not detect specific gene mutations such as JAK3 defects.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because TRECs do not measure B-cell numbers.

source.hint: These circles are excision products formed during the VDJ recombination process in the thymus.
